calls.head: Knies gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Devils keep sending Hischier’s line (Meier, Hischier and Evangelista) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Sheldon Keefe has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Blue Jackets’ first line is Knies, Bel Belluz and Johnson.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Brown has a goal and an assist as the Devils get past the Blue Jackets
paras: Timo Meier struck first for the Devils early in the first, his fourth straight game with a goal. Brenden Dillon extended the lead to 2-0 a little over three minutes later, but Charlie Coyle got the Blue Jackets on the board late in the period. Connor Brown made it 3-1 for the Devils midway through the second, and that one stood up as the winner. The Blue Jackets’ Mathieu Olivier left late in the period and didn’t return. The next day, he was placed on injured reserve. Mikael Pyyhtiä cut New Jersey’s lead to 3-2 shorthanded with 14 seconds left in the period, in his first game of the season. The Jackets’ Jack Williams picked up his first NHL point.

The Devils had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Blue Jackets 30-21. Connor Hellebuyck made 19 saves for the Devils, and Cam Talbot stopped 27 of 30 at the other end. The Devils improved to 16-8-0, second in the Metropolitan, while the Blue Jackets fell to 9-13-0, seventh in the Metropolitan.
